rationale: Evidence: all 60 development trials ended off_track (0 finishes). Progress was only 0.10 to 0.15, and max_error sat at about 0.06 m, which is the off-track limit. Steering oscillation was low (0.08 to 0.15), so the robot is not jittering. It drifts steadily off the line, which points to too little steering authority or response at 1.6 m/s, not to a gain that is too high. Line loss happened 1 to 2 times per run, so the 5-sensor array with 8 mm footprints (covering only ±2 cm, with the outer sensors often seeing no tape) is probably losing the line on bends. Changes: (1) Geometry: widen to 7 sensors spanning ±3 cm at 1 cm spacing, with 12 mm footprints, so the line stays under the array on sharper bends and the outer sensors still see tape. Sensors move slightly forward to y=0.05 for more look-ahead. (2) Controller: sensor weights scaled to [-2, -1.33, -0.67, 0, 0.67, 1.33, 2] so the signal stays inside ±2 and reflects offset in cm. kp rises from 3 to 5 for more steering authority on bends. kd rises from 0.15 to 0.3 to damp the extra gain. base_speed drops from 1.6 to 1.2 to reduce the lateral slip that carries the robot off the line. This will cost some time, so the finish needs about 1.25 m/s average over the course, and I accept that risk because completion (+500) matters most. ki stays at 0.02. Line_loss stays last_direction. Expected result: fewer line-loss events, lower max_error, and completion on oval and s-bend. Hypotheses to test: (a) the drift comes from under-steering at speed, so the speed reduction and kp increase should cut max_error below 0.04 m; (b) line loss comes from sensor coverage, so line_loss_events should drop toward 0 with 7 sensors. Measurements to check next: progress and completion_time (to see whether 1.2 is too slow), max_error and line_loss_events (to test the coverage and authority hypotheses), and steering_oscillation (to confirm kd is damping rather than causing lag).
